title: Extremally disconnected components of a finite finitely presented algebra
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings with an algebra map R -> S. Assume R is w-contractible, meaning w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], with strictly henselian maximal localizations [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and extremally disconnected connected-component space. Assume S is finite as an R-module and finitely presented as an R-algebra. Assume also that S is w-strictly-local: it is w-local and its maximal localizations are strictly henselian. Then the quotient topological space pi_0(Spec S) of connected components is extremally disconnected. The zero algebra and non-flat or nonreduced algebras are included.

source.place: Tag 0986, final paragraph, reducing the closed-point locus to Tag 0985, Lemma 61.11.5; its finite case is expanded here using the finite affine section-cover theorem (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0985).

proof.text: Let I be the vanishing ideal of the closed points of Spec R. Its zero locus is exactly those closed points because that locus is closed. The closed embedding Spec(R/I) -> Spec R identifies its domain homeomorphically with the closed-point locus, hence with pi_0(Spec R). Transport Hausdorffness and extremal disconnectedness across this homeomorphism.

For maximal p of R/I, its contraction m in R is maximal. Invert R outside m to map R_m onto kappa(p). Surjectivity follows by lifting first through R -> R/I and then through the residue map, which is surjective at a maximal ideal. This map is local. Its induced map from the separably closed residue field of R_m is injective, being a field map, and surjective by the same lift. Therefore kappa(p) is separably closed. Every prime of R/I is maximal because its spectrum is Hausdorff.

Set B=S/IS. The explicit algebra equivalence Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor identifies B with (R/I) tensor_R S as an R/I-algebra. Module finiteness and finite presentation hold by base change and transport across this equivalence. Apply the finite-algebra spectrum theorem to R/I -> B.

Integrality says a prime of S is maximal exactly when its contraction in R is maximal. Consequently V(IS) is precisely the closed-point locus of Spec S. The quotient closed embedding identifies Spec B homeomorphically with this locus. W-strict-locality of S supplies w-locality and the closed-point/component homeomorphism. Transport the extremal disconnectedness obtained in the preceding step to pi_0(Spec S). No point or nontriviality assumption is needed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0986, final paragraph; E3 formalizes the closed-point quotient, residue-field comparison, and quotient/tensor base change, reducing only the finite Hausdorff spectrum part to Tag 0985.
